headline: Approved minutes of earlier meetings; no other votes were recorded.
summary: Commissioners approved minutes of earlier meetings by unanimous vote. The agenda also listed the Hamden Police Department's August 2026 monthly report, crime statistics report, and traffic stop count report. The minutes record no other votes.
decisions: Approved minutes of earlier meetings by unanimous vote.

decision_evidence.quote: Commissioner Hampton made a motion to approve all the Police Commission minutes. Commissioner Ladore seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor.

On Saturday, August 1, 2026 the Hamden Police Department held a child safety seat inspection 
and installation.  The event was held from 9:00 AM-12:00 PM at the Hamden Police Department 
parking garage upper level. NHITSA certified Hamden police officers conduct the inspections 
and seat checks. 
 
Tuesday, August 4, 2026:

Villano Park. A collaborative Hamden Police Department event where local businesses, 
organizations and agencies come together to better serve our community.  Huge thank you to all 
involved in making this year’s event a huge success.

Incidents of Special Interest 
 
 On August 5, 2026, Jack Gill  of 90 Alston Ave, New Haven was arrested  on 3 arrest warrants.  
The warrants were the result of sexual assault allegations while Gill was working as a substitute 
teacher in the Hamden School system.  DCF and this Department were made aware of the 
allegations in early April 2026.  Each arrest warrant charged Gill with Risk of Injury to a Minor 53-
21 and Sexual Assault in the 4th Degree.  Each warrant held a $25,000 bond which Gill posted 
and he was issued a court date of 8/6/2026 at GA 7 Meriden. 
 
On Wednesday, August 5, 2026, the  New Haven Police Department was  alerted to unusual 
activity within an apartment on Edgewood Avenue.  Hamden TFO Vivenzio and a group from DEA 
New Haven District Office were summoned for their investigative expertise. 
After drafting a se arch warrant, Vivenzio and his colleagues ultimately discovered that the 
apartment was evidently being used as a clandestine lab and stash house. A significant volume 
of drugs including mushrooms, firearms, and over $80,000.00 in cash was seized.
HAMDEN POLICE DEPARTMENT

 2026 
 
 
  
 
  
 
 
 
Incidents of Special Interest (continued) 
 
 
 
 
 
On August 10, 2026 at approximately 12:15 AM , Officers responded to the area of St . James 
Street and Savoy Street on the report of shots fired.  Upon arrival, Officers spoke with a neighbor 
who reported hearing 4 gun shots.  The witness stated a light color SUV was being chased by a 
darker color SUV.  The witness stated the vehicles were exchanging gunfire befor e leaving the 
area.  The Hamden Police  Detective Division responded to handle this investigation.   This is an 
active investigation, any information should be forwarded to lead investigator Detective Palma.
HAMDEN POLICE DEPARTMENT 
MONTHLY REPORT 
AUGUST 2026 
 2026 
 
 
  
 
  
 
 
 
Incidents of Special Interest (continued) 
 
On August 15, 2026, Officers responded to 7 Mid Hill on the report of a home invasion robbery.  
The investigation revealed a juvenile had 3 juvenile friends over his house to play video games.  
During this time all 3 juvenile friends were armed with handguns.  At one point the 3 guests robbed 
the resident and stole a handgun owned by the resident’s mothe r.  The 3 juveniles then fled the 
scene on foot.  An extensive investigation was conducted by Detective Zarzuela led to identifying 
the 3 juvenile’s suspects and the application for search warrants for their ad dresses.  Over the 
last month members of Hamden and New Haven Police served all 3 warrants at 3 separate homes 
in New Haven.  The subsequent search led to the recovery of the stolen handgun along with a 
second handgun and parts to make a third.   Also recovered were various clothing items worn at 
the time of the robbery and key fobs to at least 4 stolen vehicles.  All 3 Juvenile suspects were 
arrested by New Haven Police for onsite charges.  Detective Zarzuela is continuing her 
investigation and arrest warrants for the 3 juvenile suspects will be forthcoming.
HAMDEN POLICE DEPARTMENT

 2026 
 
 
  
 
  
 
 
 
Incidents of Special Interest (continued) 
 
On August 26, 2026, TFO Vivenzio and his DEA colleagues interdicted a drug courier with 8k 
cash, 200+ wax folds of fentanyl, and additional packaged purple fentanyl. 
 
 
  
 
 
 
On August 30, 2026 , at approximately 12: 54 AM, patrol officers responded to 1409 Dixwell 
Avenue, Apartment 14B, for a report of a male who had fallen from a second -story window. The 
male, sustained significant head trauma and was transported to Yale New Haven Hospital with 
life-threatening injuries.  The male’s girlfriend, reported that the two had used fentanyl prior to the 
incident.  During the preliminary investigation, drug paraphernalia was observed inside. 
Detectives from major crimes and crime scene responded to the scene. The exact circumstances 
surrounding the fall have not been determined; however, preliminary information indicates that 
the fall may have been accidental or the result of a possible suicide attempt. Detective Miniaci is 
the lead detective for this incident.

Personnel, Staffing and Status 
 
The Hamden Police Department currently has 88 positions filled from the budgeted 103 positions.  
One Officer is on extended military leave, two officers are out injured or on light duty.  Four Officers 
graduated from the Police Academy in Milford.  Two of the Officers have completed their training 
and two are still in training status.   Sergeant Paul Calamita retired after over 20 years of service 
with the Hamden Police Department.   Officer Jenna Davis resigned after 7 years of service with 
Hamden.
